screen: TGTheme — the global colour/type palette every screen reads from
summary: TGTheme.m:212-246 declares itself as 'Telegram's own palette, read out of their design system file … drawn for Android at 360dp'. That is the wrong source. The 2013 iOS app's colours are hard-coded in the cell and assets classes, and docs/design-language/typography-colour.md already transcribes them correctly with line citations. Almost every constant in TGTheme is therefore a near-miss of a value the repo already knows, and the rulebook is right where the code is wrong.

findings.ours: Bubbles are a solid fill plus layer.cornerRadius: TGTheme.m:280-295 (bubbleMineColour #EFFEDD, bubbleTheirsColour white), TGTheme.m:431-438 (bubbleCornerRadius 12/10, bubbleBorderWidth 1), applied at TGChatViewController.m:5446.
findings.theirs: The original never fills a bubble. It stretches shipped art with a tail: Msg_In.png at leftCap 20 / topCap 15 and Msg_Out.png at leftCap 15 / topCap 15, with matching _High, _Selected and _Selected_Shadow variants.
findings.fix: images/Msg_In@2x.png, Msg_Out@2x.png, Msg_Out_High@2x.png, Msg_In_Selected@2x.png, Msg_Out_Selected@2x.png, Msg_In_High_Selected@2x.png, Msg_Out_High_Selected@2x.png are already in the repo and unreferenced by any file in src/. Add -[TGTheme bubbleImageIncoming]/-bubbleImageOutgoing returning [[UIImage imageNamed:@"Msg_In.png"] stretchableImageWithLeftCapWidth:20 topCapHeight:15] and [[UIImage imageNamed:@"Msg_Out.png"] stretchableImageWithLeftCapWidth:15 topCapHeight:15], and have TGChatViewController set a UIImageView background instead of cornerRadius+backgroundColor. Keep the flat-fill path only for the iOS7 'flat' style.

findings.ours: No chat-list date colour exists in TGTheme at all, so TGChatListViewController.m:2647 falls back to `[theme accentColour]` = #4CB3F5 flat / #517DA2 skeuomorphic — overwriting the correct literal that the cell's own initialiser set at TGChatListViewController.m:158.
findings.theirs: _dateLabel.textColor = UIColorRGB(0x337acc) — a fixed mid-blue, never the accent.
findings.fix: Add `- (UIColor *)chatListDateColour { return [self importedColour:@"accent"] ?: rgb(0x33,0x7A,0xCC); }` to TGTheme.m and change TGChatListViewController.m:2647 to use it. The row initialiser at :158 already has the right value; the theming pass at :2647 is what breaks it.

findings.ours: TGTheme has no unread-row background token; grep for 0xebf0f5 across src/ hits only TGTopicsViewController.m:975. Chat-list rows are white whether the chat is read or not (TGChatListViewController.m:2645-2646 sets text colours only).
findings.theirs: A dialog row with unread messages paints its background #EBF0F5 and darkens the preview text from #888888 to #5B646E.
findings.fix: Add `- (UIColor *)chatListUnreadRowColour` returning rgb(0xEB,0xF0,0xF5) (dark: keep listBackgroundColour lightened ~6%) and `- (UIColor *)chatListUnreadPreviewColour` returning rgb(0x5B,0x64,0x6E); set cell.contentView.backgroundColor and previewLabel.textColor from them in TGChatListViewController.m around :2645.

findings.ours: TGTheme.m:407-409 `onlineColour` returns TG_GREEN_BRIGHT1 #5ACD30, drawn as a green presence dot at TGChatListViewController.m:181.
findings.theirs: There is no green presence colour anywhere in the 2013 iOS app and no presence dot. Online is expressed as a text colour: #778698 for an online contact's subtitle in the contact list, and #E0EEFD (vs #C9DCF2 for offline) for the 'online' status line under the title in a chat's navigation bar.
findings.fix: Retire the green dot. Make `onlineColour` return rgb(0x77,0x86,0x98) for list subtitles, add `- (UIColor *)barSubtitleOnlineColour` = rgb(0xE0,0xEE,0xFD) and `- (UIColor *)barSubtitleColour` = rgb(0xC9,0xDC,0xF2), and colour the status text instead of drawing self.onlineDot.

findings.ours: TGTheme.m:139-155 `styleCell:` sets both textLabel and detailTextLabel to `[UIFont systemFontOfSize:15]`. The comment on :140 ("Their settings row: 15/18 title in black") cites a size that appears nowhere in the original.
findings.theirs: A grouped settings row is a bold 17pt black title with a 16pt regular value on the right.
findings.fix: In styleCell:, `cell.textLabel.font = [UIFont boldSystemFontOfSize:17]` and `cell.detailTextLabel.font = [UIFont systemFontOfSize:16]`. Delete the misleading 15/18 comment.

findings.ours: TGTheme.m:223 `TG_TEXT_PRIMARY rgb(0x22,0x22,0x22)`, used for the chat-list row title via primaryTextColour (TGChatListViewController.m:2645) and for message body text.
findings.theirs: Two distinct values, neither of them #222222: the dialog-list row title is #111111, and message body text is rgb(20,22,23) = #141617.
findings.fix: Change TG_TEXT_PRIMARY to rgb(0x11,0x11,0x11) and add a separate `- (UIColor *)messageTextColour` returning rgb(0x14,0x16,0x17) for bubble body text, so the two are not conflated.

findings.ours: TGTheme.m:224 `TG_TEXT_SECONDARY rgb(0x8D,0x8E,0x90)` is the single secondary colour for every preview and subtitle.
findings.theirs: #888888 flat, for both the dialog-list message preview and the contact-cell subtitle. The original also splits it three ways in the chat list: #888888 read, #5B646E unread, #536C8C when the preview is an action or a media placeholder ('Photo', 'joined the group').
findings.fix: TG_TEXT_SECONDARY → rgb(0x88,0x88,0x88). Add `- (UIColor *)chatListActionPreviewColour` = rgb(0x53,0x6C,0x8C) and use it in TGChatListViewController wherever the preview is a media/service placeholder rather than message text.

findings.ours: TGTheme.m:402-405 `typingColour` returns TG_BLUE_BLURPLE3 #70AAEA, applied at TGChatListViewController.m:2699.
findings.theirs: The 'typing…' line in a dialog row is drawn in `actionTextColor`, the same #536C8C the app uses for action previews — a desaturated slate blue, not a bright sky blue.

findings.ours: TGTheme.m:341-346 `cellDetailColour` returns TG_BLUE_SEMI8 #51AEE7 for the value on a settings row.
findings.theirs: #356596 — a dark, muted navy-blue, a long way from #51AEE7's sky blue.
findings.fix: `cellDetailColour` → rgb(0x35,0x65,0x96). While there, note the original's sibling value for a tappable grouped row's label is #516691 (TGActionMenuItemCell.m:77) and for an action/link row #0779D0 (TGBlockActionCell.m:59) — neither exists in TGTheme.

findings.ours: TGTheme.m:335-339 `timeColour` returns TG_TEXT_TIME #95999A, the colour of the timestamp inside a bubble.
findings.theirs: #232D37 — a near-black blue-grey. On a pale bubble the original's stamp reads almost as dark as the body text; ours is a light grey that nearly disappears.
findings.fix: `timeColour` → rgb(0x23,0x2D,0x37) for the light styles. The original's stamp font is `systemFontOfSize:11` with a 9pt AM/PM companion (:895-908) and `messageDateShadowColor` is nil (:918) — do not add a shadow.

findings.ours: TGTheme.m:272-277 `chatBackgroundColour` returns a flat rgb(217,222,212) for the skeuomorphic style — a value with no citation anywhere in the repo.
findings.theirs: The conversation background is not a colour at all: it is a tiled pattern image, `[UIColor colorWithPatternImage:[UIImage imageNamed:@"Linen.png"]]`, plus a stretched `ConversationBackgroundShadow.png` vignette overlay.
findings.fix: Return `[UIColor colorWithPatternImage:[UIImage imageNamed:@"Linen.png"]]` when !isFlat and no wallpaper is set. images/ ships DarkLinen@2x.png (used by TGLoginViewController.m:242) but is missing Linen@2x.png — extract it from the original bundle alongside ConversationBackgroundShadow.png. Until it is present, the flat rgb(217,222,212) at least needs a comment marking it as a stand-in, not a citation.

findings.ours: TGTheme.m:348-351 `sectionHeaderColour` returns TG_GRAY_SECTION #696A6F, a neutral grey, with no shadow and no font.
findings.theirs: Footer/section caption text is #697487 — the same lightness but distinctly blue — at `systemFontOfSize:14`, with a raised shadow of #DAE0E8 at offset (0, +1). The lift is what makes it read as engraved on the grey grouped-table background.
findings.fix: `sectionHeaderColour` → rgb(0x69,0x74,0x87); add `- (UIColor *)sectionHeaderShadowColour` returning rgb(0xDA,0xE0,0xE8) and have the section-header views set shadowOffset (0, 1) and font systemFontOfSize:14.

findings.ours: TGTheme.m:393-400 exposes `badgeColour` (#3D95D4) and `mutedBadgeColour` (#C5C9CC) as flat fills. Neither is referenced by any file in src/ outside TGTheme itself — the chat-list badge at TGChatListViewController.m:170 is clear-backed.
findings.theirs: The unread badge is shipped artwork, `DialogListUnreadBadge.png` (and `_Highlighted`), with a white boldSystemFontOfSize:14 label carrying a sunken #8091A6 shadow at (0, -1), turning #2371C2 with a clear shadow when the row is highlighted.
findings.fix: images/DialogListUnreadBadge@2x.png and DialogListUnreadBadge_Highlighted@2x.png are present and already used by TGTopicsViewController.m:21 — use the same stretched image in the chat-list badge. Delete `badgeColour`/`mutedBadgeColour` or reduce them to the label colours (#FFFFFF on shadow #8091A6, highlighted #2371C2).

findings.ours: TGTheme has no colour for the 'Alice: ' author prefix that precedes a group-chat preview, so TGChatListViewController falls back to the preview's own secondary grey.
findings.theirs: `authorNameColor = UIColorRGB(0x345f8f)` in boldSystemFontOfSize:14 — a distinct navy that separates the sender's name from the message text.
findings.fix: Add `- (UIColor *)chatListAuthorColour { return rgb(0x34,0x5F,0x8F); }` and draw the prefix in boldSystemFontOfSize:14 with it.

findings.ours: TGTheme.m:353-356 `profileHeaderColour` returns TG_BLUE_DARK3 #5A8EBD as a flat plate behind a profile picture, and is unreferenced anywhere in src/.
findings.theirs: The profile header is the linen pattern with no blue plate; the type on it is #222932 for the name and #6D7D90 for the status line, each with a rgba(#EDF0F5, 0.28) lift at (0, +1).
findings.citation: docs/design-language/typography-colour.md:139-141 citing Telegraph/Telegraph/TGProfileController.m:780-791; background via TGInterfaceAssets.mm:143-151 (`linesBackground` / SettingsBackground.png, already shipped as images/SettingsBackground@2x.png and used at TGProfileViewController.m:150)
findings.fix: Delete `profileHeaderColour` or repoint it at the pattern; add `- (UIColor *)profileNameColour` = rgb(0x22,0x29,0x32) and `- (UIColor *)profileStatusColour` = rgb(0x6D,0x7D,0x90).

findings.ours: TGTheme.m:298-307 `bubbleBorderColour` draws a 1pt rgba(0,0,0,0.12) hairline on every bubble, justified by a comment claiming 'their bubbles carry a hairline whatever the era'.
findings.theirs: There is no bubble border constant in the 2013 source. Msg_In.png / Msg_Out.png carry their own edge and drop shadow inside the artwork, and every text shadow in the bubble is explicitly nil (`messageTextShadowColor`, `messageDateShadowColor`, `messageAuthorNameShadowColor`).
findings.citation: Telegraph/Telegraph/TGTelegraphConversationMessageAssetsSource.m:180-189 (messageTextShadowColor returns nil, the alternative commented out) and :917-920 (messageDateShadowColor returns nil); bubble edge is in the art at :652,:721
findings.fix: Once the Msg_In/Msg_Out artwork is in place, bubbleBorderWidth should be 0 for the skeuomorphic style; keep the hairline only for the invented flat/dark styles, and correct the comment on TGTheme.m:301-303 — it asserts an original behaviour that the source does not contain.

findings.ours: TGTheme.m:411-415 `separatorColour` returns TG_STEEL_LIGHT3 #E1E4E9 for every list, and TGTheme.m:220 uses TG_GRAY_LIGHT3 #F7F7F7 for the sticky bar/header strip.
findings.theirs: The strip above a list is #E4E9F0 (`dialogListHeaderColor`), the hairline bracketing a highlighted contact row is #D5DEE5, and the hairline above a full-width action row is #E5E5E5. The original has no single #E1E4E9.
findings.fix: `separatorColour` → rgb(0xE5,0xE5,0xE5) for plain list hairlines; add `- (UIColor *)listHeaderStripColour` = rgb(0xE4,0xE9,0xF0) and `- (UIColor *)rowHighlightColour` = rgb(0xE9,0xEF,0xF5) with its rgb(0xD5,0xDE,0xE5) bracket.

findings.ours: TGTheme.m:212-214 documents the whole palette's provenance as 'their design system file … drawn for Android at 360dp', and TGTheme.m:215-235 names the constants after Android tokens (TG_BLUE_DARK4, TG_STEEL_LIGHT13, …).
findings.theirs: The 2013 iOS app has no design-system file; every colour is a literal in a cell or assets class, and docs/design-language/typography-colour.md:67-185 already transcribes all of them with exact file:line citations.
findings.fix: The rulebook is correct and TGTheme.m ignores it. Rename each constant after the role the iOS source gives it and cite the original file:line beside it, so the next agent editing TGTheme cannot re-derive a value by eye. This is the root cause of the twelve findings above, not a finding in its own right.
